name.description: Optional name locally unique to the parent {@link FlowGraph}. Useful for user-facing APIs such as visualization.

inTypes.description:
key - port name
value - information about type associated with this port. This is useful for {@link FlowGraph.Edge} validation.

outTypes.description:
key - port name
value - information about type associated with this port. This is useful for {@link FlowGraph.Edge} validation.

parents.description:
ids of parent vertices in {@Workflow#parent} {@link FlowGraph}. NOTE: there can be multiple in the case
that several vertices in the parent {@link FlowGraph} were merged as part of translation to a single vertex
in the new graph.

timeout.description:
Timeout for the execution of the vertex. After timeout time has passed the vertex execution fails if not
successfully completed or failed already.

defaultArgs.description: Default args to provide as input to the condition that can be overwritten by any input args (if available).

waitForTrue.description:
By default, the condition will be evaluated one time and then move to either the "$true" or "$false" step,
depending on the result.  Set this to true to wait for the result to return `true` before proceeding.  In this case
the "$false" port will never be used.  Instead the "error" port will used.  If there is an edge between the "error"
port and the "$start" port of another `Workflow.Vertex`, the the workflow will progress to that vertex without
failing the workflow.  Otherwise the workflow will fail.

Note that if this is set to true, a `timeout` must be specified to avoid the workflow from becoming permanently
stuck.

title:
A specialized workflow vertex {@link Workflow.Conditional} whose next vertex to be executed will be determined
by the evaluation of a given condition.
Every {@link Workflow.Conditional} has one default input port: "$start".

Every {@link Workflow.Conditional} has three output ports: "$true", "$false" and "error".
NOTE: this vertex type has no other output. If execution of the vertex fails port "error" will record related
information. Otherwise, the workflow execution will continue through either port "$true" or port
"$false", depending on whether the condition evaluates to true or false, respectively.
```
-------------------                         ---------------------------                     -------------------
| Workflow.Action | $success -----> $start  |                         | $true -----> $start | Workflow.Action |
-------------------                         |                         |                     -------------------
                                            |  Workflow.Conditional   |                     -------------------
-------------------                         |                         | $false ----> $start | Workflow.Action |
| Workflow.Action | out ----------->   args |                         |                     -------------------
-------------------                         |                         | error -----> ...
                                            ---------------------------
```
name: Workflow.Conditional
